distractors.reason: We don't say 'listen quickly' to mean paying attention. 'Quickly' describes speed, not the way we hear or focus.
We don't say 'listen heavily'. 'Heavily' is used with things like rain or drinking, not with listening.
We don't say 'listen strongly'. 'Strongly' describes force or belief, not attention to sounds or speech.

example_sentence: Please listen ___ to the numbers from twenty to one hundred.
l1_interference: Os falantes de português costumam colocar o advérbio antes do verbo, dizendo 'carefully listen' em vez do correto 'listen carefully'.
explanation: In English, the adverb usually comes after the verb it describes when there is no object. 'Listen carefully' is the normal order, while placing the adverb before the verb sounds unnatural.

related_collocations.example: She can speak English fluently after two years of study.
He works hard every day to pay for his course.
I always sleep well when the room is quiet.

memory_tip: The adverb usually comes right after the verb: listen carefully, work hard, sleep well
